title: What did you do yesterday?
goal: Form the regular past tense — two groups, two endings — and talk about what has happened.
bekal: form the past tense of group 1 (**-ede**) and group 2 (**-te**)
talk about what you did yesterday and last week
use past time expressions: *i går*, *i sidste uge*, *for to dage siden*
wave: Review **unit 15** first: describe three people you know, three sentences each, and make sure the adjective forms are right.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — En lang mandag
dialogs.intro: Tuesday morning in class. The teacher asks about the Monday that just went by.

lines.speaker: Læreren:
lines.text: Hvad lavede I i går? Ahmad?
lines.id: What did you all do yesterday? Ahmad?

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Jeg arbejdede hele dagen. Fra otte til seks.
lines.id: I worked all day. From eight to six.
lines.literal: I worked whole day-the. from eight to six.

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Jeg lavede mad, spiste, og så kiggede jeg fjernsyn.
lines.id: I cooked, ate, and then I watched TV.
lines.literal: I made food, ate, and then looked I far-sight.

lines.speaker: Mette:
lines.text: Jeg cyklede til Amager og besøgte min bedstemor.
lines.id: I cycled to Amager and visited my grandmother.
lines.literal: I cycled to Amager and visited my best-mother.

lines.speaker: Mette:
lines.text: Vi snakkede i to timer, og hun fortalte om krigen.
lines.id: We talked for two hours, and she told me about the war.
lines.literal: we talked in two hours, and she told about war-the.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Jeg studerede til klokken to om natten.
lines.id: I studied until two in the morning.
lines.literal: I studied to clock-the two in night-the.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Jeg glemte, at vi havde prøve i dag.
lines.id: I forgot we had a test today.
lines.literal: I forgot, that we had test today.

lines.speaker: Læreren:
lines.text: Vi har ikke prøve i dag, Budi.
lines.id: We don't have a test today, Budi.
lines.literal: we have not test today, Budi.

notes: **Two groups, two endings.** Regular Danish verbs form the past tense with **-ede** (group 1) or **-te** (group 2). There's no reliable rule for guessing the group — but group 1 is a bit bigger, and almost every new verb that enters Danish joins group 1.
**The verb still doesn't change with the subject.** *Jeg arbejdede, du arbejdede, de arbejdede*. Danish's big advantage from unit 2 holds fully in the past tense too.

**Spiste, fortalte, glemte, havde, var** — five past forms in this dialog that are **not** regular. Some look like group 2 (*spiste*, *glemte*), others clearly rebel (*fortalte*, *havde*, *var*). Unit 18 deals with them.
**Så kiggede jeg** — notice the verb-second rule from unit 10 again. *Så* takes first place, so the subject jumps behind the verb.
**At besøge** = to visit. A group 2 verb: *besøgte*.
**Krigen** = the war — in Denmark, without further explanation, this almost always means the German occupation of 1940-1945. Conversations with older Danes often touch on it.
**Det lyder interessant** = that sounds interesting. *At lyde* (to sound) is used exactly like English *to sound*.
**En prøve** = exam, test. The official Danish exams for newcomers use this word too: *Prøve i Dansk 1, 2, 3*.

grammars.title: Group 1: the -ede ending
body: The biggest group. Take the infinitive, drop the *-e* if there is one, and add **-ede**.
after: The *-ede* ending is said as one quick breath, **-uhdhuh**, almost "-uh-dhuh". In fast speech it often shrinks until it nearly disappears.
A stem with a single consonant after a short vowel doubles it before the ending: *at snakke → snakkede* (two k's), *at stoppe → stoppede*.

grammars.title: Group 2: the -te ending
body: The smaller group, but it contains many very common words — so you need to know it just as well.
after: *The last row is slipped in as a warning: *at hjælpe* looks like group 2 but is actually irregular — its past is *hjalp*. Don't guess from the shape.

Some group 2 verbs also change their vowel slightly: *at fortælle → fortalte*, *at sælge → solgte*, *at vælge → valgte*, *at bringe → bragte*, *at spørge → spurgte*. This small group is best learned as its own list — compare English *tell → told*, *sell → sold*.

A memorizing method that works: don't learn "group 1" or "group 2" as labels. Learn **pairs** — *arbejder / arbejdede*, *taler / talte* — as one whole sound. The brain stores sounds far better than categories.

blocks.text: ⚠️ Notice the different patterns with day names: **i mandags** (last Monday), **på mandag** (next Monday), **om mandagen** (every Monday). All three appeared in unit 8; now the first one finally gets used.
*For … siden* wraps around the number: *for tre dage siden*, *for en uge siden*, *for mange år siden*. Like English "… ago", but with an extra word in front.
Remember that all these expressions can stand at the start of the sentence — and once they do, the subject jumps: *I går **arbejdede jeg** hele dagen.*
Telling a story isn't just about the past tense, it's about linking events. These words do that job.
All these words take first place and **trigger the swap**: *Så **cyklede vi**…*, *Pludselig **ringede telefonen**…* If you write *Så vi cyklede*, you've broken the rule from unit 10.

blocks.title: Your first storytelling practice
items: Tell the story of yesterday in ten past-tense sentences. Use *først*, *så*, *bagefter* and *til sidst* to link them.
Then retell it about **someone else** — a friend or family member. Notice that the verbs don't change one bit. A saving that almost no other European language offers.
Then write it down. Writing reveals past-tense mistakes that slip through in speech — especially the choice between *-ede* and *-te*.
I cooked and then watched TV.
Two days ago I visited my grandmother.
I forgot we had a test today.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite with the time expression first — remember to swap the subject.
items: Jeg arbejdede hele dagen i går.
Hun besøgte sin bedstemor i sidste uge.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
items: prøve / at / glemte / vi / jeg / havde

answers: arbejdede — talte — cyklede — købte — boede — læste — snakkede — hørte

I går arbejdede jeg hele dagen. — Jeg lavede mad og kiggede fjernsyn. — Vi snakkede i to timer. — Jeg cyklede til Amager. — For to dage siden besøgte jeg min bedstemor. — Jeg glemte, at vi havde prøve i dag.
I går arbejdede jeg hele dagen. — Bagefter cyklede vi til stranden. — I sidste uge besøgte hun sin bedstemor. — Pludselig begyndte det at regne. — Til sidst tog vi hjem.
Hvad lavede du i går? — Jeg arbejdede hele dagen. — Vi snakkede i to timer. — Jeg besøgte min bedstemor. — Jeg glemte, at vi havde prøve.
